title: Assess privacy impact before a processing change
summary: Before a new or materially changed use of personal data that may carry elevated privacy risk. A reviewed assessment with mitigation owners, residual-risk approval and a recorded launch decision.
outcomes: A reviewed assessment with mitigation owners, residual-risk approval and a recorded launch decision.
guidance: Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.
when: Before a new or materially changed use of personal data that may carry elevated privacy risk.

parts.title: Describe the processing and affected people
parts.guidance: Document the purpose, data categories, people, recipients, systems and intended decisions. Map collection through deletion and identify vulnerable groups, monitoring or sensitive information for specialist review.

references.title: GOV.UK data protection and your business

execution.rationale: Prepare or reconcile the specified private evidence and documents; external changes and decisions use their own approved steps.

parts.title: Determine the assessment and consultation requirements
parts.guidance: The privacy lead and qualified advisers decide which local assessments, reviews or consultations apply. Record the criteria and applicable scope without treating a global checklist as legal approval.

references.title: GOV.UK data protection and your business

execution.rationale: The accountable person performs the decision, expert assessment or personal interaction described in this step. Supporting preparation does not authorize that act.

approval.scope: Determine the assessment and consultation requirements

parts.title: Evaluate necessity, alternatives and risks
parts.guidance: Describe less intrusive ways to meet the purpose and assess misuse, access, accuracy, security and downstream effects. Support proposed safeguards with evidence and name the owners of unresolved questions.

references.title: GOV.UK data protection and your business

execution.rationale: Prepare or reconcile the specified private evidence and documents; external changes and decisions use their own approved steps.

parts.title: Approve mitigations and residual risk
parts.guidance: Accountable owners review the assessment and required advice before authorizing the defined use. Keep launch paused for unresolved mandatory approvals or unacceptable risks and record the exact conditions of acceptance.

references.title: GOV.UK data protection and your business

execution.rationale: The accountable person performs the decision, expert assessment or personal interaction described in this step. Supporting preparation does not authorize that act.

parts.title: Verify implementation and reassessment triggers
parts.guidance: Check that approved controls, notices and contracts match the deployed system. Calendar review and reopen the assessment when data, purposes, vendors, technology or affected populations materially change.

references.title: GOV.UK data protection and your business

notes.text: This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.
